Slow smoothly and increase following distance.

Use lane markings or the right road edge as a guide without staring at oncoming lights.

If you cannot see well enough to drive, leave the roadway at a safe place and wait.

In poor conditions, make these three changes:

blocks.title: Fog needs low beams
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
High beams reflect light back.

Use low beams and reduce speed.

Never drive into unknown water.

Depth and current are hard to judge.

Turn around when the road is flooded.

Heat can hurt the vehicle.

Watch tires, temperature, and warning lights.

Never leave a child in a parked car.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: In fog, use [[low]] beams — high beams reflect back and reduce what you see.

blocks.title: Wind moves more than your car
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Expect trucks, trailers, bicycles, and debris to shift.

Hold space on both sides.

Narrow mountain roads need cooperation.

When cars cannot pass, the downhill-facing driver normally backs up.

Use a safe turnout.

When two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow road and neither can pass, the vehicle facing downhill is generally better able to back up.

The descending vehicle must yield and back up when necessary.

Use the nearest safe place rather than squeezing past.

Drive at a speed that lets you stop within the road you can see.

blocks.title: Conditions set the pace
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
If you cannot see or grip enough road, slow down or stop somewhere safe.

Never drive faster than is reasonable for darkness, fog, smoke, rain, glare, or traffic.

Keep stopping distance within the visible usable path.

If you cannot see enough road to stop safely, reduce speed further or leave the roadway at a safe place.

lessons.title: Skids, Blowouts, and Vehicle Failure
lessons.objective: Smooth control matters most when the vehicle stops behaving normally.

intro.summary: Smooth control matters most when the vehicle stops behaving normally.
keyPoints: Move people away from greater danger.

blocks.title: What would you do?
blocks.scenario: A front tire suddenly blows out.

blocks.title: A blowout needs calm hands
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Grip the wheel firmly.

Keep the car pointed where you want to go.

Emergency questions often offer a dramatic action that feels decisive.

The safer answer usually stabilizes first and avoids adding a second failure through panic steering or braking.

blocks.title: Do not slam the brakes
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Ease off the accelerator.

Slow gradually before leaving the road.

The first seconds are about keeping the vehicle stable.

Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle pointed straight.

Slow gradually, signal, and move off the roadway when safe.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: Blowout? [[Grip]] the wheel, ease off the gas, and do not [[slam]] the brakes.

blocks.title: A skid means lost grip
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Look toward the safe path.

Ease off the cause and steer smoothly.

When traction is lost, avoid sudden braking, acceleration, or steering.

Look toward the intended path and recover control progressively.

A large correction can send the tires past available grip in the opposite direction.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: In a skid, ease off the cause, look toward your intended [[path]], and steer [[smoothly]].

blocks.title: Different skids need different corrections
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Avoid one memorized steering slogan.

Use the vehicle handbook and modern stability systems correctly.

Mechanical failures feel different, but the first priority is remarkably consistent: keep the vehicle stable, communicate, reduce exposure, and stop in the safest available place.

blocks.title: Off the pavement? Slow first
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Hold the wheel steady.

Return at a shallow angle only when speed and traffic allow.

A fast steering correction can turn a small drift into a loss of control.

Ease off the accelerator and hold the wheel firmly.

Brake gently if needed while keeping the vehicle straight.

Return to the pavement gradually when speed and traffic allow.

blocks.title: Brake failure needs options
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Try controlled braking, a lower gear, and the parking brake gradually.

Look for a safe escape path.

Keep control first, alert others, and identify a safe escape.

The exact vehicle-specific action can differ, so use the owner manual for equipment details; do not apply a memorized sequence that assumes every vehicle has the same system.

blocks.title: A roadside stop is still dangerous
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Pull fully away from traffic.

Use hazards and stay protected when possible.

When a collision threat develops, reduce speed and choose the path that preserves control while protecting people.

An empty shoulder may be better than a crowded lane; a controlled impact may be better than a violent swerve into pedestrians or opposing traffic.

blocks.title: Emergency order
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Hold the steering wheel securely, avoid a panic brake, and reduce accelerator pressure progressively.

Correct only enough to stabilize the vehicle.

Once control and speed allow, signal and move to the safest available place away from traffic.

When the vehicle fails, keep this order:

lessons.title: After a Crash
lessons.objective: Protect people first. Reports and insurance come after immediate safety.

intro.summary: Protect people first. Reports and insurance come after immediate safety.

blocks.title: What would you do?
blocks.scenario: A crash causes an injury.

blocks.title: Stop after a collision
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Do not leave the scene.

Move out of traffic when the law and safety allow.

A collision scene can create a second crash.

Stop and remain at the scene as the law requires.

Call emergency services for injuries or immediate danger.

Move vehicles only when safe and appropriate, and warn approaching traffic when possible.

blocks.title: Check people before property
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Call 911 for injury or immediate danger.

Give reasonable help without creating another hazard.

A collision creates several separate duties: protect people, stop, provide information, give aid, and make the correct later reports.

Police, DMV, and insurance steps are not interchangeable.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: Stop, check [[people]] first, exchange [[information]] — never leave the scene.

blocks.title: Exchange the required information
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Share identification, vehicle, and insurance details.

Stay calm and factual.

After an injury or fatal crash, stop and share the required information.

Give reasonable help.

Arrange medical transportation when needed or requested.

The required written report to CHP or local police is due within 24 hours unless a qualifying officer report has been made.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: After an injury or death, the written police report is due within [[24 hours]].

blocks.title: An unattended car still creates duties
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Leave the required notice.

California may also require police notification.

After a property-damage-only collision, stop and provide the required identifying information.

If the owner cannot be found, leave the required written notice and notify police as California law directs.

Leaving because the damage looks small can turn a crash into a failure-to-stop offense.

blocks.title: Police and DMV reports are different
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
One report does not automatically replace the other.

Check every trigger.

Different agencies use collision information for different purposes.

Exchange the required driver, vehicle, and insurance details.

Report to law enforcement when the circumstances require it.

File the DMV collision report when California’s injury, death, or property-damage threshold is met, even if another person also reports.

blocks.title: California uses separate clocks
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Report a crash to DMV within 10 days if someone is injured or killed.

The same deadline applies when one person has more than $1,000 in property damage.

A reportable driver who cannot provide required financial-responsibility evidence can face DMV suspension procedures.

Keep the reporting deadlines separate:
bullets: An injury or death can trigger a 24-hour police report.
A reportable collision can trigger a DMV report within 10 days.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: Report to DMV within [[10 days]] after injury, death, or more than [[$1,000]] damage to one person.

blocks.title: Insurance follows its own process
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Document the scene when safe.

Notify the insurer and keep records.

Do not swap 24 hours and 10 days.

The shorter period is the injury/death written police report; the 10-day period is the DMV report when its trigger applies.

blocks.title: Remember the order
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Drivers and owners must be able to establish financial responsibility.

For policies or bonds issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025, California uses updated minimum liability limits.

They are $30,000 for one person's injury or death, $60,000 for two or more, and $15,000 for property damage.

After a collision, keep these actions in order:

title: The Driver and the Vehicle
outcome: Manage impairment, distraction, passengers, and vehicle safety.

lessons.title: Phones, Fatigue, and Road Rage
lessons.objective: Driving needs your eyes, hands, judgment, and emotional control.

intro.summary: Driving needs your eyes, hands, judgment, and emotional control.

blocks.title: What would you do?
blocks.scenario: A message arrives while you are driving.

blocks.title: Distraction has several forms
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Your eyes can leave the road.

Your hands or mind can leave driving too.

A driver can lose the road with eyes, hands, hearing, mind, or judgment.

Device laws set minimum boundaries; safe attention often requires doing less than the maximum a device technically allows.

blocks.title: Set up before moving
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Choose navigation, music, mirrors, and temperature first.

Then put the phone away.

A conversation can take attention even when your hands remain on the wheel.

Set navigation and music before moving.

Let a passenger handle tasks or pull over safely.

Do not read, type, eat, reach, or handle objects when it takes your eyes or mind from driving.

blocks.title: California limits device use
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Adult mounted use is narrow and hands-free.

A long task is not allowed because the phone is mounted.

A mounted wireless device may be operated only under California law's placement and single-swipe or single-tap conditions.

A long message, search, video, or repeated input does not become acceptable because the mount is legal.

blocks.title: Drivers under 18 have stricter rules
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
California generally prohibits device use, even hands-free.

The law treats a genuine emergency differently from ordinary phone use.

A driver under 18 may not use a wireless telephone or electronic communication device while driving, even hands-free, except for emergency purposes.

Do not borrow the adult mounted-device rule for a minor-driver question.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: An adult may use a phone only [[hands-free]], activated with a single [[swipe or tap]].

blocks.title: Fatigue can copy impairment
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Heavy eyes, missed signs, and drifting are warnings.

Coffee may increase alertness briefly, but it does not replace sleep.

An adult driver may not use a handheld wireless telephone while driving.

Any permitted voice communication must satisfy hands-free conditions and legal exceptions.

Holding the phone at a red light is not a reliable way around a rule tied to driving.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: A driver under 18 may not use a phone while driving — even [[hands-free]] — except in an emergency.

blocks.title: Stop before you nod off
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Leave the road at a safe place.

Rest or change drivers.

A prohibited driver-visible video display, both ears covered, severe fatigue, or willful disregard can each destroy safe observation and control.

Stop the trip when fatigue prevents timely decisions.

Reckless driving is more than a small mistake; it involves a conscious disregard for safety.

blocks.title: Road rage is a choice you can exit
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Do not chase, block, stare, or argue.

Create distance and call for help if threatened.

Legal placement is not legal attention.

The exam may describe a mounted phone but then add repeated taps, reading, video, or a minor driver—facts that change the answer.

blocks.title: Your condition is part of safety
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Angry, sick, dizzy, or exhausted? Do not drive until you can focus.

Illness, strong emotion, poor sleep, vision changes, and medicine can reduce judgment or reaction.

Read medicine warnings and ask a professional when effects are unclear.

Do not drive when drowsy, dizzy, angry, or unable to focus.

Avoid covering both ears with a headset or earplugs while driving.

lessons.title: Alcohol, Drugs, and Medication
lessons.objective: A legal substance can still make driving unsafe and illegal.

intro.summary: A legal substance can still make driving unsafe and illegal.

blocks.title: What would you do?
blocks.scenario: A prescription warns that it may cause drowsiness.

blocks.title: Impairment starts before you feel drunk
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Judgment and reaction can change early.

Feeling normal is not proof of safe driving.

It is unlawful to drive while under the influence of alcohol, a drug, or their combined influence.

Prescription or legal status does not excuse impaired control.

If a substance prevents safe driving, do not drive.

blocks.title: Time removes alcohol
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Coffee, food, air, and showers do not sober you quickly.

Plan another ride.

Never calculate a “safe number of drinks.” Body response varies, and the course has no formula that converts drinks into permission to drive.

Plan a sober ride before drinking.

blocks.title: California has several BAC rules
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
The adult per se level is 0.08%.

Lower rules apply to drivers under 21 and people on DUI probation.

Read age and probation facts before choosing a number.

Match the limit to the driver and situation:
bullets: The adult per se rule is 0.08%.
A person under 21 has a 0.01% preliminary-screening rule and a separate 0.05% offense.
A person on DUI probation has a 0.01% rule.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: Adult per se limit: [[0.08%]]. Under 21, zero tolerance starts at [[0.01%]].

blocks.title: Cannabis can impair driving
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Legal purchase does not make impaired driving legal.

Using cannabis with alcohol or another drug can increase impairment.

Judgment, attention, vision, coordination, and reaction can worsen before a person notices.

Coffee, food, a shower, or fresh air does not quickly remove alcohol.

Cannabis and medicines can impair driving even when legally obtained.

Combining substances can make the effect stronger and less predictable.

blocks.title: Medication counts too
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Read warnings.

Ask a professional when the effect is unclear.

A driver and passenger generally may not drink an alcoholic beverage in a motor vehicle on a highway, subject to passenger-area exceptions.

You must not possess an opened alcohol container or specified opened cannabis while driving, subject to legal storage and vehicle exceptions.

blocks.title: A DUI arrest can trigger chemical testing
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Refusing a required test can create consequences separate from the DUI case.

The exact rule depends on the legal situation.

By driving in California, you agree to certain chemical tests after a lawful DUI arrest.

The available tests and conditions depend on California law.

Refusing or failing to complete a required test triggers administrative consequences; a first refusal carries a one-year period.

blocks.title: Open containers have their own rules
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Keep alcohol and cannabis where California law allows.

The passenger area is restricted.

The reliable plan is made before impairment starts.

Choose a sober driver, transit, taxi, or rideshare.

Never ride with a driver you believe is impaired.

Keep alcoholic beverages and cannabis containers where California law allows; an open container does not belong in the passenger area.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: An open container never rides in the [[passenger area]] — keep it where the law allows.

blocks.title: Make the decision before using
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Do not negotiate after impairment starts.

DUI questions become easier when you separate impairment, status-based BAC rules, chemical testing, and container rules.

A number can prove a specific violation; it never guarantees that the person is safe to drive.

blocks.title: Can you finish the rule?
blocks.ruleMarkdown: By driving in California, you consent to [[chemical testing]] after a lawful DUI arrest.

lessons.title: Protect Everyone in the Car
lessons.objective: Belts, child restraints, airbags, and supervision work together.

intro.summary: Belts, child restraints, airbags, and supervision work together.
keyPoints: Never leave a child in danger.

blocks.title: What would you do?
blocks.scenario: A car has airbags. Does everyone still need a seat belt?
blocks.questionPreview: Does everyone still need a seat belt?

blocks.title: Seat belts work on every trip
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Buckle before the car moves.

The driver must also protect passengers under California law.

Drivers and passengers in covered vehicles must be properly restrained by an available safety belt, subject to legal exceptions.

A short trip, low speed, or rear seat does not make an unrestrained occupant safe.

blocks.title: Wear the belt correctly
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Place the lap belt low across the hips.

Keep the shoulder belt across the chest.

An airbag is designed to work with correct seating and restraint.

Sit upright and keep a safe distance from the airbag cover.

Use the rear seat and the correct child restraint for young passengers.

blocks.title: Airbags are extra protection
blocks.bodyMarkdown:
Sit upright and keep space from the cover.
